biggest_catch: This is a business card: you need a real business activity to apply, even a sole proprietorship or freelance work, and you sign a personal guarantee, so the debt is yours. Year-one math: 100,000 Ultimate Rewards points are worth at least $1,000 as cash back, minus the $95 annual fee, which leaves roughly $905 net in the first year. Only claim this if your business was already going to spend $8,000 in 3 months on normal purchases; never spend extra to hit the target. Chase states the new-cardmember bonus may not be available if you have ever had this card, and may consider factors pertinent to your business when deciding bonus eligibility. Chase's unpublished 5/24 pattern also applies to business-card applicants.
catches: Only claim this if your business was already going to spend the money anyway; never spend extra just to hit the $8,000 minimum, because manufactured spending turns a bonus into debt.

Year-one math: 100,000 points are worth at least $1,000 as cash back, minus the $95 annual fee, which leaves about $905 net in the first year. From year two the $95 fee applies without a bonus, so keep the card only if its 3x travel, shipping, internet, cable, phone, and advertising categories beat that $95 on your real business spending.
Applying triggers a hard credit inquiry on your personal credit report, and you sign a personal guarantee, so the business-card balance is legally your personal debt if the business does not pay.
This card's APR is around 20% or higher, so carrying a balance would wipe out the bonus fast. Pay the statement balance in full every month or this offer loses you money.
Chase's unpublished 5/24 pattern: five or more new personal cards opened in the last 24 months generally means denial, even for business-card applicants with excellent credit.

Chase states the new-cardmember bonus may not be available to you if you have ever had this card, and that it may consider factors pertinent to your business in determining bonus eligibility. Do not open a second Preferred expecting the bonus again.
You need a genuine business activity to apply, including an eligible sole proprietorship or freelance operation. A personal guarantee means the issuer can pursue you personally for the balance.
The account must be open and not in default when the bonus is paid, and the bonus is paid only once per account.

steps: Go to the official Chase Ink Business Preferred page and read the current offer headline and the Pricing & Terms before anything else.
Confirm you have genuine business activity (a sole proprietorship or freelance work counts) and understand you will sign a personal guarantee.
Apply online as the business, using your personal details as guarantor. Expect a hard inquiry on your personal credit report.
Use the card for the business purchases you were already planning, totaling at least $8,000 in the first 3 months after account opening.
Pay the statement balance in full every month; do not carry a balance at the ~20%+ APR.
Allow 6-8 weeks after the spending requirement is met for the 100,000 points to post, and confirm they appear in your Ultimate Rewards account.
Before the second $95 annual fee hits, check whether the card's 3x business categories earned you more than $95 in real value in year one, and downgrade or cancel if not.
